report.summary: SetFileInformationByHandle with FILE_RENAME_INFO_EX and FILE_RENAME_POSIX_SEMANTICS provides genuine POSIX rename-over-open-file semantics on Windows 10 1709+ on NTFS and ReFS: the rename is immediate and all open handles reflect the new name. Cross-volume renames are not atomic; fallback to MoveFileEx is required. SMB support requires protocol-level POSIX extensions (SMB 3.1.1+ with appropriate server capabilities). FAT/exFAT do not support it. Atomicity is maintained locally but may be impacted by memory-mapped files or oplocks.
risks: Only available on Windows 10 version 1709 and later; call will fail with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER on older releases.
Fails on SMB shares unless the server supports the SMB 3.1.1 POSIX extensions and the share is configured appropriately—many NAS devices do not support this.
Not supported on FAT/exFAT volumes; may fail or behave unexpectedly.
Memory-mapped files or files with active oplocks can prevent the rename even with the POSIX flag (observed in some edge cases).
Renaming across volumes is not atomic and requires a copy/delete fallback (MoveFileEx with MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED).
Atomicity guarantees are not fully documented for all failure modes; no published formal verification.
todos: Use FILE_RENAME_POSIX_SEMANTICS for local renames on NTFS/ReFS when the file may be open; fallback to FILE_RENAME_INFO (delayed rename) for broader version compatibility.
Implement a pre-check for cross-volume rename and use MoveFileEx with COPY_ALLOWED, noting the lack of atomicity.
Test SMB behavior against target server OS versions; check for SMB dialect and POSIX extension support via GetFileInformationByHandleEx or WMI.
Add assertion that the volume is not FAT/exFAT before attempting POSIX rename.
Consider detecting memory-mapped sections via NtQueryVirtualMemory and aborting the rename if unmapping is not possible.
Measure rename latency under load to verify no regressions; no published benchmarks exist, so instrument the code.

handoff.suggestion: Add a test harness that opens a file with FILE_SHARE_DELETE, renames it using the POSIX flag, and verifies that the original handle still refers to the file at the new path. Repeat on NTFS, ReFS, and an SMB share with known POSIX extension support. Document the exact Windows build numbers and fallback paths.

name: q02-posix-rename-semantics
question: Does SetFileInformationByHandle with FILE_RENAME_INFO_EX and FILE_RENAME_POSIX_SEMANTICS (Windows 10 1709+) give true POSIX rename-over-open-file semantics, and what are its limits on NTFS, ReFS and SMB shares?
